    "As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site," Bahrain's Ministry of Interior noted on X. The ministry later said two people, a Bahraini citizen and a Pakistani resident, were injured in the attack.

    Bahrain is home to the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet.

    In a recent development, iranian state media reported late Saturday that the country's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired missiles and drones at U.S. military facilities in Bahrain.

    According to recent reports, A separate Iranian media report claimed the IRGC's air defenses intercepted and destroyed a U.S. MQ-9 drone.

    U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on either Iranian report.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi remarked his government remains open to a negotiated settlement to the war. An agreement aimed at developing a permanent peace deal signed in June between President Donald Trump and his Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian — the so-called Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding — later broke down.

    "The Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding is no longer on the table and has no implementation relevance," Araghchi told the Iran newspaper.

    "However, the commitments that the U.S. had accepted in that Memorandum of Understanding and the principle that the implementation of those commitments can pave the way for reaching a final agreement are still accepted by both sides," he said.

    In a recent development, the war, which began with U.S. and Israeli airstrikes on Iranian targets on Feb. 28, has resulted in major disruptions to energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz between Iran and Oman.

    The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported that two tankers near Oman were struck by unidentified projectiles on Saturday.

    Iran has imposed curbs on vessels moving through the strait, a major sticking point in negotiations with the U.S.

    It has been revealed that oil prices have fallen for three straight weeks, however, as traders weighed strong Middle East flows and rising U.S. inventories.

    According to recent reports, international benchmark Brent crude fell 3.4% for the week, while U.S. crude tumbled 5.2%.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (536 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Broncos, ESPN, Fox Sports and others honor longtime linebacker, analyst Tom Jackson after his death

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (536 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The NFL world honored longtime Denver Broncos linebacker and ESPN analyst Tom Jackson on Sunday, days after his death.
    • Jackson died Friday, friend and colleague Chris Berman announced Sunday during ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown." He was 75.
    • Jackson spent 14 seasons in the league with the Broncos from 1973-1986.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NFL world honored longtime Denver Broncos linebacker and ESPN analyst Tom Jackson on Sunday, days after his death.

    Jackson died Friday, friend and colleague Chris Berman announced Sunday during ESPN's "Sunday NFL Countdown." He was 75.

    Jackson spent 14 seasons in the league with the Broncos from 1973-1986. He earned three Pro Bowl nods and appeared in two Super Bowls with the franchise. He retired with 191 games played in his career, which was the fourth-most in Broncos history. Jackson, who played at Louisville before landing in the NFL, was inducted into Denver's Ring of Fame in 1992.

    The Broncos honored Jackson ahead of their game with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, and played a video tribute to him on the scoreboard at Empower Field before kickoff.

    Lee Corso, who coached Jackson at Louisville, called him the "best football player I ever had.".

    Sources indicate that "Not only that, he was the best leader I ever had," Corso remarked in a statement. "My condolences to Tom's family in this difficult time.".

    It has been revealed that after his playing career ended, Jackson joined ESPN in 1987 and promptly became a fixture in the network's NFL coverage. He worked there for nearly three decades until he retired in 2016, and spent nearly the entire time working alongside Berman.

    It has been revealed that "All of us are stunned. We've lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet," Berman noted. "I was fortunate, as you know, to work side-by-side with him for 30 years on 'NFL Primetime' and 'NFL Gameday,' now 'Sunday NFL Countdown.'".

    "Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst," he added. "There was nobody kinder, there was nobody more thoughtful, more loyal, more engaging than Tom Jackson.".

    Industry observers note that jackson was behind the iconic "Jacked Up!" segment each week during the NFL season, which showcased the hardest hits throughout the league. The segment was eventually phased out as concern for head trauma and serious injury grew throughout football.

    ESPN brought that segment back Sunday, and ended it with a huge hit of Jackson's.

    Fox Sports also honored Jackson during its coverage, and played the "NFL Primetime" music while showing halftime highlights Sunday.

    NFL commissioner Roger Goodell issued a statement remembering Jackson:.

    "The NFL lost a wonderful man with the passing of Tom Jackson. Along with millions of fans, I will always remember him as a player and broadcaster, but also as a friend. He was an outstanding player whose toughness and leadership helped define an era of Broncos football. He brought credibility, passion and humor to everything he did, and generations of fans came to know him through his work at ESPN. Tom helped fans enjoy and better understand football, always bringing the perspective of someone who loved the game and the people who play it. More importantly, he earned the respect and friendship of players, coaches and everyone who had the privilege of knowing and working with him.".

    Rich Eisen, Keyshawn Johnson, Tedy Bruschi, Randy Moss, Adam Schefter, Bill Cower and plenty of others in the NFL media world all honored Jackson and spoke about him on their respective platforms.

    #119246. Industry News: Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (515 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (515 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • According to recent reports, implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting significant moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    According to recent reports, implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the company that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the company's after-market report on Tuesday.

    According to recent reports, since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is right now 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    Sources indicate that with bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1268 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic’s record IPO collides with tech’s worst week on Wall Street since 2020

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1268 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Startup investor Ben Narasin is so jazzed about Anthropic's blockbuster IPO that he's planning a party later this month at his Silicon Valley home.
    • "This is a celebration of the most material, significant, and mind-blowingly awesome event that has ever happened in venture capital," Narasin, founding partner of Tenacity Venture Capital, told CNBC in an interview, adding that he didn't even invest in the company.
    • Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and an additional $26 billion from tech giants that bought at the offer price.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Startup investor Ben Narasin is so jazzed about Anthropic's blockbuster IPO that he's planning a party later this month at his Silicon Valley home. Sake, vodka and Krug Champagne will be served. Each attendee will be given two jars of caviar.

    "This is a celebration of the most material, significant, and mind-blowingly awesome event that has ever happened in venture capital," Narasin, founding partner of Tenacity Venture Capital, told CNBC in an interview, adding that he didn't even invest in the company.

    Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO and an additional $26 billion from tech giants that bought at the offer price. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, lifting Anthropic's market cap to $1.8 trillion and providing a much-needed windfall for Silicon Valley's startup ecosystem.

    It was quite the split-screen moment on Wall Street, which spent the week in an AI-driven tailspin. Led by Nvidia's 23% plunge, which marked the stock's sharpest weekly pullback in 18 years, the Nasdaq slid 10% over the past five trading days in its worst week since the early days of Covid in 2020.

    Investors and analysts spent the week debating whether Anthropic will trade alongside AI hardware, as it's reliant on advanced chips, memory and data centers, or whether it will stand alone as the first public pure-play AI developer and a manufacturer that's achieved unrivaled growth in less than six years of existence.

    Industry observers note that that question will likely persist for some time, but Friday's market action highlighted that Wall Street is skeptical of Anthropic's ability to grow into its lofty valuation. At week's end, the Claude creator's $1.6 trillion fully diluted market cap put it behind just six U.S. companies: Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Nvidia, Amazon and SpaceX.

    With the tech market in turmoil due to rising interest rates, raging anti-AI sentiment and Nvidia's C-suite crisis, Anthropic's IPO was part exuberance, part relief for an industry hungry for exits.

    Sources indicate that after venture-backed IPOs yielded $73 billion in proceeds in 2021, the amount raised in the next four years totaled just $39 billion, according to data from University of Florida emeritus professor Jay Ritter. In 2021, 126 technology companies went public, compared with 34 in 2025.

    Meanwhile, the private market has continued to balloon, with companies raising ever-larger sums at sky-high valuations without the pressures of quarterly earnings. Many startups that had hoped to go public early in the decade fell out of favor in the AI boom. They experienced hefty job cuts, down rounds and acquisitions for pennies on the dollar.

    According to recent reports, "There was a time in Silicon Valley not that long ago where the prevailing wisdom was the default path should be avoiding going public for as long as possible," remarked Somesh Dash, a general partner at venture firm IVP. The view was, "it's too long, it's too hard, it's not worth it," he said.

    In a recent development, anthropic is very young compared to some of those companies, but it was a huge collector of private capital. Investors poured $141 billion into the AI lab as of September, according to Anthropic's prospectus.

    For a few Silicon Valley firms that contributed to those funding rounds, the returns are unlike anything they've ever seen. At the IPO price, Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed Venture Partners each owned about $25 billion worth of Anthropic stock. Bessemer Venture Partners owned a stake worth roughly $10 billion, partner Byron Deeter said.

    Matt Murphy, a partner at Menlo, told CNBC's David Faber on Thursday that his firm has more than five limited partners "that we delivered over $1 billion of returns to.".

    According to recent reports, "At the end of the day, that's really our job, is to get dollars back into foundations and endowments," Murphy mentioned. "There's a lot of pride in being able to do that.".

    Bessemer's Deeter was also jubilant on Thursday, posting on X that, in addition to being "the largest bet in Bessemer's history," the IPO "is a punctuation mark in the history of both humanity and computation.".

    Industry observers note that that's quite a change from a few years earlier, when Anthropic was hardly generating revenue, and success was far from guaranteed. In 2023, Anthropic's Claude 2 was struggling to keep pace with models from Google and OpenAI. In April 2024, investors at Bessemer wrote in a memo that if Anthropic missed its own targets, there was "a good chance that we lose all or part of our money.".

    Guru Chahal at Lightspeed told CNBC that Anthropic was clearly the team taking a more measured approach to AI. The tech giant looked beyond Nvidia's dominant AI chips, choosing to use alternatives from Amazon and Google as well. Anthropic noted it generated $1.72 in revenue per dollar spent on computing power in the third quarter, up from 68 cents a year earlier.

    It has been revealed that "It is true that it required lots of capital, but when you dig in and you realize that capital is going toward compute, and this is the team that's positioned to use that compute in the most effective way, then we could connect those dots," Chahal noted. He added that those metrics showed it was "going to be a very high-quality business.".

    Anthropic isn't the only big win for VCs this year.

    Recent findings suggest that five months before Anthropic's Nasdaq debut, SpaceX hit the market in what, until this week, was by far the largest IPO in history. SpaceX, which Elon Musk founded in 2002, produced outsized returns for firms including Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz.

    In a recent development, spaceX and Anthropic alone will make 2026 a monster year for the venture industry, easily exceeding any other year in IPO proceeds. And investors in OpenAI hope appetite remains strong for trillion-dollar companies next year, as the ChatGPT maker is looking to 2027 for a potential offering.

    IVP's Dash noted that in his AI portfolio, "a lot of companies are starting IPO prep" even if it's only "year four, year five, year six since inception." He hopes to see at least half a dozen companies go public at valuations north of $10 billion each in the second half of 2027.

    The macro picture, however, is ominous.

    In a recent development, jensen Huang's sudden departure from Nvidia has left the chip giant without a clear leader at a time when the organization already faced heightened concerns about a slowdown in spending. Nvidia is a key investor in Anthropic and OpenAI and a critical supplier and financing partner for the entire AI industry, which is getting hammered across the board.

    In January, Democrats will take control of the House and Senate after this month's midterm elections, which included the passage of numerous ballot measures that could stymie data center development. Anthropic investor Brad Gerstner predicted after the election that market dynamics would push Anthropic to price toward the lower end of its range.

    Narasin said he wasn't even sure the organization would get that far.

    "I was concerned they'd delay," Narasin stated.

    That makes the outcome that much more impressive, he said, after Anthropic priced above its expected range and upsized the offering.

    It has been revealed that "This will be bedtime stories for years for future VCs," Narasin said. "There was a organization that was created, backed by angels and later venture" that in a few short years "became the single biggest IPO of all history.".

    — CNBC's Ari Levy contributed to this report.

    WATCH: I like owning Anthropic over the long term, says Gabelli Funds' John Belton.

    Industry News: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warns Americans of 'bumps in the road' after tech outages

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.
    • Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.
    • Clayton, however, mentioned on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.

    Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.

    Clayton, however, mentioned on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.

    "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton noted.

    "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he said.

    In a recent development, clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, which lasted for hours.

    The Federal Aviation Administration remarked router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack.

    Separately, Microsoft mentioned the Outlook outage was caused by "an glitch during an earlier network capacity upgrade.".

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' "Face the Nation.".

    Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent remarked: "No, they shouldn't.".

    "The patches may cause a glitch," he said, referring to measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency.".

    • Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.
    • Sources indicate that the report claims that "after the U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the tech giant "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    Sources indicate that the report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the company kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also said that latest export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    In a recent development, the allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    Industry observers note that "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson remarked in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    In a recent development, lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the organization's recent earnings call that China is an "key" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    #119230. Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (746 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic was supposed to save the AI trade. What went wrong?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (746 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S.
    • The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.
    • Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a significant win for the manufacturer and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Recent findings suggest that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and said it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the substantial indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    Recent findings suggest that "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he noted.

    Part of the challenge, Niles said, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," said JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he said, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    Industry observers note that anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan mentioned. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the company in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    Sources indicate that "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he mentioned. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    One bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    #119212. Latest Update: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a big buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (414 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest was a big buyer of Anthropic as she tells CNBC she’s ‘quite optimistic’

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (414 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • According to recent reports, "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence organization in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    According to recent reports, "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    Anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    "We're climbing a wall of worry," noted Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, fresh technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    The Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood mentioned she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    According to recent reports, in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the massive losses.

    It has been revealed that the fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    In a recent development, "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she remarked. "That's how crazy things were.".

    #119210. Industry News: Fantasy Football Week 11 RB Report: Another fumble makes D'Andre Swift tough to trust, plus more backfield splits

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1235 w)
    📖 Baca

    Industry News: Fantasy Football Week 11 RB Report: Another fumble makes D'Andre Swift tough to trust, plus more backfield splits

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1235 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that let's take a second to appreciate the backup running back and the importance of having that insurance on your bench.
    • If you're a Walker manager who was smart enough to add Johnson back after Week 8, nice work.
    • According to recent reports, in this piece, we talk a lot about backfield splits and depth running backs, specifically, in an attempt to inform you for future weeks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that let's take a second to appreciate the backup running back and the importance of having that insurance on your bench. Emmett Johnson drew another start in place of the injured Kenneth Walker III on Sunday. For the third time in four weeks, the rookie back went for 22+ fantasy points on a hefty 23 carries for 105 yards and a score, plus four catches for 38 yards. Most of that damage was done well before the game clock wound down in the fourth quarter.

    If you're a Walker manager who was smart enough to add Johnson back after Week 8, nice work. If you were like me (in one league) and didn't grab Johnson to replace Walker, well … it's been a rough watch the past month or so.

    According to recent reports, in this piece, we talk a lot about backfield splits and depth running backs, specifically, in an attempt to inform you for future weeks. Let's see what the highlights and box scores show us that we can use for fantasy football going into Week 12 and the Thanksgiving week slate.

    It was an ugly week in general for the Bears offense in a spot we thought could produce points, considering the team had an implied total around 30. Instead, we got inconsistency, particularly in the run game despite the return of Kyle Monangai. He had missed the past five games due to turf toe and a thumb injury. This was also an elite matchup for running backs; New Orleans entered Week 11 allowing the sixth-most rushing yards per game and sixth-most rushing TDs this season.

    While Swift got to an OK floor for fantasy purposes because of a short TD catch, he could be back in the doghouse after another lost fumble, his third of the season. As a result, we saw carries for fourth-string RB Salvon Ahmed, with Roschon Johnson leaving the game early due to an ankle injury. Monangai also wasn't his usual efficient self, though we're willing to give him a pass coming back after a long absence.

    Let's talk about Swift first. In games following a Swift fumble, Swift maintained a heavy workload with 22 touches in Week 3 and 13 in Week 5 (no Caleb Williams). So Swift shouldn't lose his role, but he also hasn't been all that impressive. He doesn't have a carry longer than 15 yards since Week 1 and doesn't have a catch that went for more than 13 yards since Week 2. Ben Johnson could opt to lean more on Monangai, but he and Swift have had a relatively even split of the carries when both are healthy, with Swift being more of a threat in the passing game. Ahmed also didn't look all that bad and could leech a few touches.

    Sources indicate that the next two weeks aren't ideal, either. The Bears get the Lions on Thanksgiving on the road and the Jaguars in Week 13, two of the worst matchups for RBs in fantasy. It will be tough to count on both Swift and Monangai as anything more than flex options in the short term, and after that we could see the latter take on more work if he can stay healthy. The matchups soften a bit in a key stretch from Weeks 14-16.

    Maybe it was the Panthers defense but the Ravens offense looks revived with Jacoby Brissett under center. At least for fantasy purposes. Baltimore scored 33 points and had over 400 yards of offense Sunday in the narrow loss to Carolina. For real life, it was brutal. For fantasy managers, it was a sigh of relief for those with Henry and Zay Flowers.

    But we're here to talk about the backfield specifically, where Henry got back to work with his highest total on the ground since Week 5, when he went for over 100 yards rushing. He now has four total TDs in the past three games and a useful nine catches in the past two. A lost fumble put a minor dent in his final total as well.

    It has been revealed that despite getting back on track the past two weeks, at least from a fantasy points perspective, there's still cause for concern for Henry managers. And it's in the form of Hill.

    In a recent development, the backup RB put together another strong outing, nearly reaching 100 total yards on just 10 touches with a 19-yard TD before halftime. Hill also had a 36-yard long rush in the game that resulted in a fumble just before scoring. All in all, he continues to showcase major-play ability. He entered the game averaging 6.8 yards per carry and had 11.5 per against the Panthers. That's going to keep Hill involved.

    Sources indicate that looking ahead, how Baltimore performs down the stretch could play a factor in how this backfield looks for fantasy managers. With six straight losses, sitting at 4-7, the Ravens aren't entirely out of the playoff picture. They still have four division games left (two against the Steelers). But a few more losses could sink Baltimore and that could lead to less work for Henry and more for Hill. We recommended Hill in the early waiver piece going into Week 12.

    It has been revealed that henry is still an RB2 for fantasy but there's also the Week 13 bye — not ideal. Hill has shown he can be an RB3/flex with upside. If you have Henry, you need Hill on your bench. If you're looking for a potential league-winner late in the season, Hill has that upside if the chips fall right.

    Kamara can't keep getting away with this, can he?

    According to recent reports, last week, it was a tilting five touches for 14 total yards and two scores. This week, it's just TWO yards on two touches, but another touchdown. Seven other carries went to various skill position players and QB Tyler Shough. But at least it was a decent showing by Etienne in his second game back after being placed on injured reserve after Week 3.

    It wasn't the most encouraging performance by Etienne but it was good enough for his managers to trust him back in their lineups. Most of his 76 yards came on a 46-yard run, but that's fine; we wanted to see Etienne get back to making big plays, and that was his biggest of the 2026 season. The volume was also a great sign with Audric Estimé a healthy scratch for Week 11; the backfield was all Etienne's.

    The larger issue is the Saints offense. It's not performing up to par, like the boat races and shootouts we saw in flashes last season after Shough took over. The O-line isn't great and Shough has regressed a bit. The rest of the fantasy schedule lines up well for points (at CIN, vs. GB, at CAR), which is a plus. But we need to see some progress from Kellen Moore's group overall in order to have faith in Etienne as an RB2.

    The back has that potential but he'll need 15-20 touches and a few big plays mixed in. Etienne is going to lose snaps to Kamara and New Orleans likes using the vet in the red zone. This game has us putting Etienne back in the RB2/3 range, while Kamara is only a risky, TD-dependent flex in PPR.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (436 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (436 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • In a recent development, if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    In a recent development, if Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the upcoming tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    According to recent reports, implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders substantial and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," said Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time.     AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Prediction markets outlook for stocks in 2026 dims amid AI sell-off

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (268 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.
    • Recent findings suggest that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026.
    • Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    Recent findings suggest that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note stated.

    Industry observers note that the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    According to recent reports, in that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

    Latest Update: The Nasdaq is in freefall. Here's one stock to look at

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market.
    • Recent findings suggest that amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years.
    • It has been revealed that AWS demand supports the lower end of the range.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market. Its advice was surprisingly useful: avoid panic selling and look for opportunities. A 40 VIX, which it touched Friday, might provide those opportunities. Specifically, a higher VIX (higher options premiums) signals fear, but it also creates an opportunity to sell elevated premium in some premium stocks, like Amazon.

    Recent findings suggest that amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years. AWS revenue rose 39.3% YoY in the third quarter, and management reported a $578 billion backlog. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow rose 29% to $168.3 billion. However, infrastructure investment accelerated, resulting in more than $42 billion in negative cash flow. The competing forces of accelerating growth and the cost of supplying it could keep the stock in its range over the next four weeks. Its shares are only off 14% from its recent highs, comparatively better than the Nasdaq Composite's near 19% decline.

    It has been revealed that AWS demand supports the lower end of the range. The backlog gives Amazon a basis for adding capacity even as investors scrutinize the cash cost. Cash spending could temper an upside rerating.

    The next leg higher may require evidence that latest capacity can earn attractive returns at this scale, and that evidence may be in short supply over the next couple of months.

    Recent findings suggest that sell the Dec. 18, 2026 AMZN 235/285 strangle for an indicative $5.90 credit per share.

    Max reward — $590 per strangle if AMZN finishes between $235 and $285 at expiration, before fees.

    Breakevens at expiration — $229.10 and $290.90.

    Max risk — Unlimited on the uncovered call, but one should think of the trade as risking getting short at a net price above $290, a nearly 13% premium to today's closing price. The downside loss would reach $22,910 per strangle if AMZN fell to zero. The credit is roughly 2.3% of a $260 reference share price over four weeks, or nearly 30% on a simple annualized basis. That comparison uses the share price as its denominator. Actual return on capital depends on margin and the cost to close or settle the trade.

    Buying in bear markets, as the Nasdaq just touched, is never easy. But those opportunities don't present themselves too often. What are you going to do with it?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, investors often favor dividend stocks for their regular income and the promise of potential share price appreciation. But selecting the right dividend stocks from a huge pool of companies can be difficult.

    Top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend-paying stocks, as their recommendations are backed by thorough analysis of a firm's financials.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    It has been revealed that devon Energy (DVN), an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company, reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. The company announced a quarterly dividend of 32 cents per share for the fourth quarter, payable December 30. Based on the fixed dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, DVN yields 2.85%.

    Sources indicate that after hosting a virtual investor meeting with management, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Devon, with a price target of $59. Mehta said that he is now more confident in management's outlook for delivering strong near-term capital returns as well as efforts to drive operational efficiencies and productivity gains.

    Sources indicate that devon sees an opportunity to increase share repurchases, driven by solid free cash flow (FCF), contributions from the Eagle Ford divestiture and continued improvement in the balance sheet, Mehta said. Devon expects share buybacks worth more than $1 billion in Q4 2026, up from $414 million in the third quarter, backed by a strong pricing backdrop and improved capital efficiency.

    Recent findings suggest that mehta, a 5-star analyst, stated Devon expects about $6.3 billion of excess FCF in 2027, including about $3.5 billion of net proceeds from the Eagle Ford sale. That would enable the organization to accelerate buybacks while progressing toward its goal of reducing gross debt to about $9 billion by early 2027. Mehta noted that under DVN's framework to return up to 70% of annual FCF, management favors share buybacks as it believes the stock is discounted compared to large-cap peers.

    "Management expects continued capital efficiency gains from merger synergies, extended laterals, surfactant adoption and development of the newly acquired federal acreage," Mehta mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that mehta ranks No. 876 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.1%. See Devon Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Recent findings suggest that energy Transfer (ET), is a limited partnership that operates about 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. The company recently declared third-quarter results showing net income per common unit growing about 18% year-over-year, to 33 cents. ET's cash distribution for Q3 2026 was 34.25 cents per common unit, up more than 3% year-over-year. At an annualized distribution of $1.37 per share, Energy Transfer yields more than 7%.

    TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer with a price target of $25. The organization delivered better-than-expected Q3 results and unveiled the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d) South Mississippi Pipeline, a 215-mile, 36-inch natural gas line linking the Perryville Hub to the Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) network, Gabelman remarked. The project is supported by 20-year firm transportation agreements and is expected to enter service in 2030. ET expects to ultimately own 51% of the $1.6 billion project.

    The 5-star analyst mentioned that Energy Transfer lowered its 2026 capital spending outlook to $5.5 billion (midpoint of the guidance range) from $5.75 billion due to project timing. Energy Transfer expects capex to rise to $7 billion in 2027, while Gabelman projects $5 billion in both 2028 and 2029, based on disclosed projects.

    Industry observers note that gabelman also highlighted management's commentary about optimization initiatives contributing an incremental $800 million to 2026 earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a larger benefit than in recent years. "A return to less commodity volatility should the [Middle East] war end could bring some relative downside, though this is offset by continued strong growth prospects," he stated.

    Gabelman ranks No. 397 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15.4%. See Energy Transfer KPIs on TipRanks.

    Oil and gas exploration and production company ConocoPhillips (COP) delivered better-than-expected Q3 performance. The company confirmed an 11% hike in its quarterly dividend to 93 cents per share, effective with the Q4 dividend payable on December 1. Based on the dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, COP yields about 2.6%.

    Following the Q3 results, Wells Fargo analyst Sam Margolin repeated a buy rating on ConocoPhillips, citing strong potential for further dividend increases. Margolin also trimmed his price target to $185 from $189 to reflect timing effects and the WAHA forward curve, though he said that COP could still re-rate as its natural portfolio lifecycle provides stronger protection against inflationary pressures than peers. The Waha forward curve tracks future natural gas prices based on the West Texas Waha hub.

    Margolin, another 5-star analyst, highlighted that ConocoPhillips' Q3 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $3.27 was well above Wells Fargo and the Street's estimates of $3.04 and $3.05, respectively. Earnings were driven by solid price realizations, partially offset by higher depletion, depreciation and amortization and purchased commodities.

    Margolin also noted COP's dividend increase and mentioned the accelerated buyback enabled by current commodity prices could further support long-term dividend growth. He sees the possibility of ConocoPhillips' dividend growth rate exceeding its current 6% cost of equity into the end of the decade. Margolin expects COP to sustain an 8% dividend compound annual growth rate through 2029 while repurchasing $6.4 billion of stock annually, and reducing net debt-to-capital to less than 9% by the end of 2028 based on the assumption of an average Brent crude oil price of $75 a barrel.

    "The message on the 3Q call was similar to that of 2Q, reiterating the moderation in reinvestment rate and commitment to dividend growth through the Willow start-up and after," Margolin said.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Week 11 of the NFL's Sunday schedule is off to a solid start, with seven games officially in the books for the early window and three games left to go in the afternoon.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Week 11 of the NFL's Sunday schedule is off to a solid start, with seven games officially in the books for the early window and three games left to go in the afternoon.

    According to recent reports, the early slate was dominated by a couple of blowouts — including a 51-30 win by the Dallas Cowboys over the Tennessee Titans (a scorigami!). Dak Prescott shined with a near-perfect passer rating, throwing for 325 yards, 4 touchdowns and no interceptions.

    The biggest surprise of the afternoon slate was the entertainment offered by the Baltimore Ravens and Carolina Panthers. Carolina's 35-33 win over Baltimore offered plenty of chaos, including a fumble through the end zone, a muffed punt and more, as Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard rumbled for 120 yards and two scores on the ground.

    Sources indicate that closing out Sunday's slate, the San Francisco 49ers (8-1) seek to maintain the NFL's best record as they face the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) in Mexico City. Receiver Mike Evans is listed as questionable but is expected to play.

    Jets vs. Chargers, 4:05 p.m. on Fox.

    Raiders vs. Broncos, 4:25 p.m. on CBS.

    Steelers vs. Eagles, 4:25 p.m. on CBS.

    Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more from Week 11's Sunday game slate.

    Breaking: Cowboys open game with 6 straight touchdowns, rip Titans in Dallas

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Dallas Cowboys did not have the worst defense on the field for a game this season, but the story Sunday was their offense.
    • According to recent reports, the Cowboys demonstrated some improved defensive execution in Sunday's 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans, although it was mostly in comparison to their opponent's defense.
    • The only failures: A Brandon Aubrey field goal and the Cowboys kneeling down to end the game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Dallas Cowboys did not have the worst defense on the field for a game this season, but the story Sunday was their offense.

    According to recent reports, the Cowboys demonstrated some improved defensive execution in Sunday's 51-30 victory over the Tennessee Titans, although it was mostly in comparison to their opponent's defense. Dallas scored touchdowns on its first six offensive possessions of the game and scored on their first eight series in the blowout at AT&T Field.

    The only failures: A Brandon Aubrey field goal and the Cowboys kneeling down to end the game.

    According to recent reports, dak Prescott was nearly perfect against the Titans' harried defense, throwing for 325 yards and four TDs and rushing for another score. Prescott's rushing score gave the Cowboys their sixth TD in as many possessions.

    Recent findings suggest that it was Prescott's second straight game accounting for five TDs. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both caught TD passes, and Javonte Williams had one score each receiving and rushing.

    Dallas' shortest drive before the fourth quarter was 56 yards. A Titans defense that saw multiple starters dealt prior to the trade deadline had little chance to slowing down the Cowboys.

    According to recent reports, the Cowboys (5-6) stayed within range of the first-place New York Giants (5-3-1) in the NFC East. The Titans dropped to 1-9, still in line to earn the top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft as of now.

    Dallas' incremental improvements defensively Sunday came with caveats, including Carnell Tate's 59-yard touchdown reception in which four Cowboys defenders failed to touch Tate while he was down.

    Industry observers note that another hiccup was allowing ex-Cowboys running back Tony Pollard to run for 110 yards, at 5.2 yards per clip. There were also some costly penalties on the Cowboys' defense, which made a play-calling change from Christian Parker to Mike Pettine.

    Recent findings suggest that but there were positives. Dallas sacked Cam Ward five times, including a strip sack, and held the Titans to 112 first-half yards while building a three-score lead.

    The Cowboys came out aggressively, winning the coin flip and opting to take the ball first. After converting a fourth-and-2 from inside the Tennessee 5-yard line, Williams punched it in for the first score. Dallas went for 2 and failed.

    The Titans kicked the first of three first-half field goals to cut the lead in half, but the Cowboys struck back on KaVontae Turpin's 22-yard rushing score.

    Dallas got the ball back and chewed up more than six minutes on its next TD drive, capped by Prescott hitting Lamb on a gorgeous throw in the back of the end zone.

    It has been revealed that the Titans settled for two more field goals to close out the first half. Prescott's TD pass to Pickens made it 27-9, Dallas, at halftime.

    Ward called his own number on an audible on the Titans' opening drive, sneaking it in for a rushing touchdown on Tennessee's opening drive of the second half. But the Titans never made it less than a two-score game the rest of the way.

    According to recent reports, the Cowboys beat the Titans 51-30 on Sunday. This final score is what is colloquially known as Scorigami, meaning that it is the first time this final score has occurred in NFL history.

    Tennessee went down fighting. With 31 seconds left in the game, quarterback Cam Ward found Calvin Ridley for the 12-yard score.

    The Titans scored 30 points, but it will not be enough after the impressive display the Cowboys put on today.

    The Cowboys offense has dropped a 50-burger.

    Recent findings suggest that after the long fumble recovery, Dallas needed just three plays for paydirt. Cowboys tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford caught Dak Prescott's fourth touchdown pass of the game, this one for two yards.

    The Cowboys now lead 51-23 with just under five minutes to go.

    The Dallas defense finally had a massive play to go along with how dominant the offense has been today.

    Quinnen Williams obliterated Cam Ward from the blind side and the Titans quarterback fumbled it.

    The ball bounces around, before a Cowboys corner finally picks it up and runs it 70 yards, flipping the field.

    The Cowboys have finally gone a drive without scoring a TD. Dallas previously was 6-for-6 scoring a touchdown on each of its six drives to open the game against Tennessee.

    Finally, the Titans defense kept the Cowboys out of the end zone.

    Instead, Brandon Aubrey nailed the 49-yard field goal.

    Dallas now leads 44-23 with 11:33 left to go in the game.

    Sources indicate that tennessee watched as Dallas scored its sixth touchdown on as many drives. The Titans got a first down, but then had two incompletions, a sack and a delay of game.

    This resulted in Tennessee choosing to punt down 41-23 with 2 minutes left in the third quarter.

    The Cowboys offense has been perfect against the Titans. Dallas has had the ball six times and has scored six touchdowns.

    The most recent came from Dak Prescott keeping the ball. He ran to the right and scored the 2-yard touchdown. Prescott just broke the plane of the goal line and the score was confirmed.

    Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate had a wild 59-yard touchdown against Dallas.

    Tate went to the ground, but managed to get his body off the ground by the time the Cowboys defenders got to him. The rookie was touched by Dallas defenders, but since he was off the ground, he took off for the end zone after the defense left him alone.

    Tate scored the TD, and the play was reviewed nd he was confirmed to be off the ground when touched.

    Dallas has had the ball five times against Tennessee, and has now scored five touchdowns.

    Javonte Williams scored his second of the day as he took a pass from Dak Prescott 11 yards for the score.

    Sources indicate that tennessee's offense got the break it needed during halftime. The Titans ran only four plays and benefited from a 38-yard DPI call.

    Regardless, on first and goal from the 1, Cam Ward dove for the end zone after taking the snap and broke the plane of the end zone for the score.

    The Cowboys take a 27-9 lead into halftime.

    It has been revealed that tennessee's offense got down the field, but simply ran out of time. Cam Ward spiked the ball with 1-second left on the clock.

    Sources indicate that this set up a 28-yard field goal for Joey Slye, which he made. Slye has all of the Titans' points so far, with three field goal makes.

    Dallas' Big 3 has each found the end zone now. After Javonte Williams and CeeDee Lamb had already scored, George Pickens finally got his.

    Dak Prescott threw the ball over the middle and found Pickens for the 10-yard score.

    It has been revealed that dallas' defensive strategy may just be to score a TD on every possession and hope that is enough. At the moment, on Sunday, it is as the Cowboys lead 27-6 with just over four minutes left in the first half.

    Tennessee ran six plays and picked up only 18 yards, but it was enough to get into field goal range.

    Titans running back Tony Pollard picked up 19 yards on three carries, but a sack and an incompletion brought up fourth-and-eight on the Dallas 30.

    Sources indicate that joey Slye came out for the 48-yard field goal attempt and nailed it. Tennessee trails 20-6 with 10:34 left in the first half.

    It looked like Dak Prescott was throwing the ball away under pressure from the Tennessee defense.

    Prescott was rolling right and just barely got the pass off. It looked destined for out of bounds, but then CeeDee Lamb came into frame and the pass was perfectly placed for Lamb to not only grab it, but also get the necessary two feet in for the score.

    Tennessee's offense was clicking on its first possession of the game, but not the second.

    The Titans had a five-yard run on first down, lost a yard on a Carnell Tate reeption on second down and then Cam Ward was sacked by Justin Houston on third down.

    The quarter ended, but when the second quarter starts, the Titans will be punting.

    While the Dallas defense has struggled, the offense is firing on all cylinders. The Cowboys picked up 74 yards on six plays, including a touchdown run by wide receiver KaVontae Turpin.

    The speedster showed off his wheels and went around the left end for a 22-yard score.

    Dallas didn't go for 2 this time and just let Brandon Aubrey knock through the extra point. The Cowboys lead 13-3.

    One of the main stories this week was Dallas DC Christian Parker losing play-calling duties to Mike Pettine while remaining the DC.

    Dallas' defense went with a bend-don't-break approach on Tennessee's first drive of the game.

    Industry observers note that cam Ward hit Chimere Dike for a 22-yard gain, then later had an 8-yard reception. Running back Tony Pollard picked up 13 on a carry.

    The Titans got into the redzone but were unable to find the end zone. Instead, Joey Slye knocked through a 38-yard field goal to make it 6-3, with the Cowboys in front.

    Tennessee's challenge of the first down was not successful.

    Recent findings suggest that dallas got the fresh set of downs and ran Javonte Williams twice. On the second attempt, the running back forced his way into the end zone for the score.

    The Cowboys opted to go for two because of a penalty giving them a closer attempt, but it failed.

    Dallas has been grooving its way down the field against Tennessee.

    In a recent development, facing fourth and short, the Cowboys kept the offense on the field and went for it. Quarterback Dak Prescott kept the ball for a quarterback keeper, and it looked on the broadcast that he had easily gotten it.

    Tennessee head coach Robert Saleh wasn't convinced, though, and tossed an early challenge flag. The ruling was upheld — first down, Cowboys.

    Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate will return to the active lineup for Tennessee in Week 11, officially active for the first time since Week 7 after dealing with a shoulder injury.

    Despite having missed two games, Tate leads the team with 413 receiving yards this year with a single receiving touchdown. His presence will be key this week, especially after teammate Wan'Dale Robinson was placed on season-ending injured reserve with an ankle injury this week.

    #119156. How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1404 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1404 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light.
    • Let's take a look at four major reasons.
    • Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light. It initially came against weaker opponents, with wins over the Pacers, Clippers, Jazz and Kings getting them back near .500. But these back-to-back wins over Cleveland (on Friday) and Detroit (on Saturday) put a real stamp on this stretch. After all the panic, Miami has won seven of nine and is tied for the East's No. 4 seed entering this week.

    How have they turned things around? Let's take a look at four major reasons.

    Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins. The concerns over their offensive fit -- as relative non-shooters who operate largely in the same spots -- have quieted, but also a good bit of this production is coming independent of one another as Erik Spoelstra is staggering their minutes between the start of each half and fourth-quarter closing time.

    With shooters all around, Adebayo and Antetokounmpo are free to attack maximum interior space and exploit soft midrange spots, which has been the bread and butter of this run.

    Every mid range jumper from Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo against Cleveland last night: pic.twitter.com/jeamVaSLhk.

    Recent findings suggest that as pointed out by Couper Moorhead of NBA.com, the Heat face more drop-coverage defense (when the substantial who's guarding the ball screener falls back toward the rim rather than stepping up to the level of the screen or even higher to contest the shooter coming off the screen) than any other offense in the league. That's because nobody fears Miami's pull-up 3-point shooters, and because Giannis and Bam are such forceful attackers of the rim.

    Recent findings suggest that the soft spot is in between, outside the restricted circle but inside the 3-point line, or even better inside the free-throw line. It's the dreaded midrange zone, where defenses are happy to, concede shots to players like Giannis and Bam, and right now they are both knocking these supposedly inefficient looks down at ridiculous rates.

    These are by far career-high percentages for both guys, and they are coming on career-high frequencies from these zones (over 30% of their total shot attempts in the 3-10 range). Over these last nine games, Giannis is a scorching 22 for 33 from 10-19 feet while Adebayo -- who has also been the best post scorer in the league at 1.26 PPP on 4.8 post-ups per game -- is 30 for 44 from 5-14 feet.

    They are absolutely wearing these outer-paint shots out, and if defenses keep with the drop coverage, these shots are likely to remain consistently available. It's not to say they'll keep making them at this rate, of course. But to have established these go-zones is a massive step for Miami's half-court offense, because we all know how dangerous they are in the open floor as the highest-frequency and second-highest-scoring transition team.

    Now add in the fact that Miami kills teams on the glass with Giannis and Bam on the court (over these last nine, they are grabbing 78.7 percent of all available defensive rebounds and 37.8% of all offensive rebounds, both of which would lead the league), and in the turnover battle, and what you have is a Heat team that is getting a lot more true shot attempts than its opponents (almost 10 more per 100 possessions).

    In a recent development, that is everything in today's possession-obsessed NBA. Get up more shots than your opponent by generating second-chance opportunities on the offensive boards and by creating more turnovers than you cough up, and you're in a good spot. Make those extra shots at the rate Miami is right now, and you're almost unbeatable.

    It has been revealed that mitchell has gone from a guy perhaps playing to stay in the league, or at least in an NBA rotation, to a current top-three Most Improved Player candidate at FanDuel (+900). He's blowing his previous production away.

    It has been revealed that the Heat are a low-volume pick-and-roll team for the same reasons they're a prime candidate for drop coverage: They don't have those kinds of pull-up shooters. Mitchell can punish drops with pull-up 3s on occasion (8 for 20 so far, per Synergy), but more importantly he's the one most often hitting Bam and Giannis in those soft-pocket midrange spots we talked about -- in addition to the rim rolls, cuts and kick-out 3s that open up as he breaches the paint, often in transition.

    Recent findings suggest that of Mitchell's 119 assists so far, 55 have gone to Giannis and Bam, and he has directly set up a 3-point make 37 times. Those 9.2 assists per game lead the league among qualified players, and the 257 points his assists have generated rank second only to Trae Young's 260, per PBP Stats. Young is making $49 million this year. Mitchell is making $12 million.

    Then there is the shooting. Mitchell has steadily improved from range throughout his career, but this season he's on fire at 43% on catch-and-shoot 3s, per Synergy, as part of Miami's spacing around Bam and Giannis. We saw all of Mitchell's tools in his 22-point/17-assist masterpiece against Cleveland.

    Davion Mitchell ABSURD statline vs Cavs: 22 PTS | 5 REB | 17 AST | 7/14 FG | 66 TS% pic.twitter.com/b0d8I1XHDy.

    Thompson isn't the player he was in his prime. His defense has especially declined, and he's not going to be putting up any more 37-point quarters. But he's still a sniper.

    In a recent development, thompson is splashing 42% on almost 10 3s a game, and his 48 total 3-pointers rank third league-wide, and his 15.3 PPG are the most he's averaged since leaving Golden State. He's been especially hot of late, averaging 20 PPG on 48/45 shooting splits over his last seven games.

    Klay Thompson was amazing vs the Pistons26 PTS - 4 AST - 6 3PM - 10/17 FGM Found a new home pic.twitter.com/JvQju9Hais.

    According to recent reports, over the last seven games, Miami is plus-11.7 with Thompson on the court and minus-3.7 when he's off. That's the best split on the team. The starting lineup of Mitchell, Bam, Giannis, Thompson and Pelle Larsson (who has been substantial in this turnaround, too, since his promotion to the first five), the Heat are outscoring opponents by 23 points per 100 possessions, and Thompson has been particularly effective playing alongside Giannis. With those two on the court as Bam rests, Miami is drumming teams by 31.6 points per 100, per Databallr.

    In a recent development, miami's defense was expected to be a strength, and when people looked up and saw a bottom-barrel rating, it was jarring. Some of that, if not most of it, could be attributed to inordinately hot shooting by their opponents, which wasn't likely to continue. And indeed it hasn't.

    Through the first seven games, Miami opponents were shooting 41.8% from 3 and 50% from the midrange, per Cleaning the Glass. That made for a 58.7 effective field-goal percentage, despite Miami's defense registering a top-three expected eFG% (52.9) based on the shots they were surrendering, per Cleaning the Glass.

    Recent findings suggest that translation: the Heat were, and are, forcing generally inefficient shots, but to start the year those shots were going in at a rate of almost 6% better than expected. That was the worst, or unluckiest, mark in the league, however you want to look at it.

    Cut to this four-game win streak, over which opponents are down to 35.2% from 3 with a 53.9 eFG% against an expected 54%, per CTG. That's in part because Miami has cut the number of wide-open 3s (nearest defender at least six feet away) it was allowing to start the year almost in half (to start, they were surrendering 16 wide-open 3s every night, but over this four-game winning streak they are down to 9.1, stingiest in the league). Even better, their opponents have come down from a 45.5% conversion rate on those wide-open 3s to 40%.

    In a recent development, all of which is to say, Miami's opponent shooting is coming back to earth. Hot shooting can render any defense helpless, but over time, if you're forcing a team into tough shots from tough spots, the averages are going to swing back your way eventually. Miami is starting to see that happen.
